title: "pak reinstalls packages already present in another library"

categories: [renv and installation]

attendu: "nothing to install, the dependencies are already there"

::: {.piege .piege-statique}
```r
.libPaths()
# [1] "~/R/library-personal"
# [2] "/opt/R/library-shared"

pak::pkg_install("mypackage")
```
:::

This pitfall depends on several libraries and the network, so it cannot be replayed in the browser.

## Why

{pak} installs into a single library, the first one in `.libPaths()` by default, and reasons about the contents of that library. A dependency already installed in the shared library, further down `.libPaths()`, does not count: {pak} downloads it and installs it again in the personal library.

`install.packages()` behaves differently, which is surprising when you switch from one to the other. On a shared server, every user ends up with their own copy of packages the administrator had installed for everyone.

## The remedy

Since {pak} 0.9.3, pass every library to `lib`: the first one remains the target, the others are used to satisfy dependencies without reinstalling.

::: {.piege .piege-statique}
```r
pak::pkg_install("mypackage", lib = .libPaths())
```
:::
